key_insight: A hybrid GNP/C60 epoxy topcoat plus CNT surface treatment substantially improved adhesion, barrier protection, wear resistance, and superhydrophobicity on HVOF-metallized CFRP.
engineering_relevance: This approach offers a practical path to make sprayed metallized CFRP coatings more durable and multifunctional for harsh-service aerospace and structural applications.
method: Applied a graphene nanoplatelet/fullerene C60 reinforced epoxy coating onto HVOF-metallized CFRP.
Used CNT-based surface modification to tune wettability and surface functionality.
Evaluated morphology, adhesion, tensile properties, abrasion, impedance, and ice-response performance.
evidence_signal: The coated system increased pull-off adhesion from 320 psi to 650 psi, raised tensile strength from about 25 MPa to 56 MPa, reduced abrasion mass loss by over 50%, and achieved water contact angles above 155° after CNT treatment.
watch_item: Performance gains were shown under laboratory conditions, so long-term durability, process repeatability, and scale-up effects on real components still need validation.
paper_title: Hybrid Graphene Nanoplatelet/C60 Nanocomposite Modification of HVOF-Metallized Carbon Fiber-Reinforced Polymer Coatings to Improve Adhesion, Barrier Performance, and Surface Functionality
